mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined every week for the last three weeks (-13.4 to -17.7). Since commute trips chain into adjacent retail and dining visits, continued erosion of workplace attendance mechanically reduces incidental RETAIL_REC footfall over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell monotonically from -13.4 to -17.7 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days rises relative to the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to decline, indicating decoupling of commute and retail trips.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility drops below -20 percent of baseline and continues falling week-on-week by more than 2 points, reduced transit access constrains discretionary trips to retail and recreation destinations, pulling RETAIL_REC lower over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -20 and week-on-week change exceeds -2 points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -20.0 at t-0w after a -0.7 point weekly drop
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks even though TRANSIT remains below -20 and keeps declining.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects a broader behavioral retreat from out-of-home activity; the joint effect compounds beyond either series alone, suppressing RETAIL_REC more strongly than either factor would individually over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT declined in each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 28 days is no larger than predicted by WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, i.e., no amplification is observed when both decline together.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated and volatile PARKS mobility (44.9 to 51.9) indicates households substituting outdoor recreation for indoor retail and recreation trips during summer, which will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS averaged above 44 percent for all four weeks in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days even while PARKS remains elevated above 40 percent, showing no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: The correlated weekly declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT without a corresponding rise in RESIDENTIAL suggest voluntary health-caution behavior (e.g., response to a circulating wave) rather than formal lockdown; this caution regime will keep RETAIL_REC suppressed over the coming week before any rebound.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed near 0 despite falling WORKPLACES and TRANSIT
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within the next 7 days despite continued WORKPLACES and TRANSIT declines and flat RESIDENTIAL, contradicting the caution-driven suppression mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has trended downward from 8.9 to 6.4 percent over the snapshot, signaling a general easing of essential-trip activity that typically co-moves with discretionary RETAIL_REC visits, implying continued decline over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 8.9 to 6.4 over the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM continues to decline, indicating the two series have decoupled.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC itself has declined in three of the last four weeks (-12.1 to -13.7); once a mobility series shows three consecutive weeks of negative momentum, behavioral inertia and habit formation make continuation of the decline likely in the immediate next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC has declined for 3 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell week-over-week from -12.1 to -12.4 to -13.9 before a slight uptick to -13.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC reverses and rises in the next week despite the preceding three-week negative momentum, breaking the inertia assumption.

mechanism_narrative: High, stable PARKS activity combined with flat RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests people are neither confined home nor avoiding all outings; this interaction indicates sustained overall mobility capacity that will spill over into modestly higher RETAIL_REC visits as summer outings extend to shopping and dining over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stayed above 44 while RESIDENTIAL stayed near 0 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 28 days even though PARKS remains elevated and RESIDENTIAL stays flat, indicating no spillover from outdoor to retail activity.
